paper.title_en: Resonance-dominated heavy-ion fusion and structures with negative components in the representation <math><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>E</mi><mi>σ</mi><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>E</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> of the fusion cross section
paper.abstract_en: The true ion-ion interaction governed by the repulsive electrostatic potential and the attractive nuclear potential at small separation is approximated as a Coulomb barrier decorated by an attractive <math><mi>δ</mi></math>-shell potential placed under the barrier. This composite potential can generate unbound or resonance states with positive energy eigenvalues. The resonances are determined through the calculation of scattering phase shift <math><mi>δ</mi></math> of the S matrix. We make the <math><mi>δ</mi></math>-shell potential complex with an attractive imaginary part in it and obtain the phase shift <math><mi>δ</mi></math> as a complex quantity. This complex phase shift gives nonzero positive reaction cross section to be considered as fusion cross section <math><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>f</mi></msub></math> in the calculation. Resonances generated by our model potential combination are clearly manifested as positive peaks in the variation of <math><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>f</mi></msub></math> as a function of energy E. The presentation of <math><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>f</mi></msub></math> as <math><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>E</mi><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>E</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></math> in variance with E shows oscillations or structures with several peaks and valleys including valleys of negative values. The calculated results of <math><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>f</mi></msub></math> and <math><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mi>E</mi><msub><mi>σ</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><msup><mi>E</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></math> are shown to account for the respective measured results showing oscillatory structures with remarkable success in the fusion data of the <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>12</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>12</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math>, <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>12</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math>, <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>16</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math>, and <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Ca</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>40</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Zr</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mrow><mn>90</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>94</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>96</mn></mrow></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> systems involving light as well as heavy nuclei.
